name: southern chickpea soup
instructions:
The house for STOCK-BASED chickpea soups — 'southern' as in southern european — the chickpeas themselves are enough to place it there, as opposed to the indian curry side of the chickpea family ([[chana-masala]], [[himachali-chana-madra]]). Two variants:

=== VARIANT A — CHICKPEA + ESCAROLE (THE FAMOUS ONE) ===

The famous italian chickpea-and-escarole soup. Stock-based, chickpeas + escarole as the identity pair. To be filled in when cooked.

=== VARIANT B — CHICKPEA + TOMATO/BELL PEPPER + CHARD STALKS ===

INGREDIENTS:
- chickpeas
- yellow onions (yellow only, I think — see notes)
- garlic
- swiss chard — STALKS BETTER THAN LEAVES (the secret ingredient, see notes)
- bay leaf
- CHICKEN STOCK (required — see the stock note)
- tomato — FRESH, necessary (canned is too saucy; see notes)
- tomato paste
- bell pepper
- olive oil
- salt and black pepper

No other seasonings or dairy required.
notes:
=== SCOPE — STOCK-BASED, SOUTH OF FRANCE + ITALY ===

This recipe houses the stock-based southern-european (french/italian) chickpea soups. VARIANT B IS VERIFIED AND GOOD — it carries the excellent tag. Variant A (escarole) is planned but not yet attempted — log results when cooked.

=== THE BIGGEST NOTE — YOU NEED THE CHICKEN STOCK ===

Chicken stock is required. I experimented with splashes of vegetable, chicken, and beef broth before deciding CHICKEN BROTH is the right ingredient. Regular vegetable stock isn't flavorful enough on its own, and dark roasted / beef stock doesn't make sense as the base.

SPLASHES OF THE OTHER STOCKS FOR DEPTH: vegetable and beef broth are SECONDARY for exactly this purpose — a splash cut into the chicken base might add depth (or use up veggie stock / make it taste different). This is deliberately a STOCK-FOCUSED soup — that's what makes it different from a straight italian tomato-chickpea soup with parmesan.

THE BALANCE: it should be MORE CHICKEN-STOCK-FLAVORED THAN TOMATO-FLAVORED overall — otherwise it turns into a SAUCE.

=== FRESH TOMATO NECESSARY — NOT CANNED ===

Same rule as [[minestrone-soup]] and [[mushroomed-lentils-italian]]: FRESH tomato is necessary. Canned doesn't work as good — too saucy. A BOX OF CHERRY TOMATOES is usually perfect — they're lighter.

=== SWISS CHARD STALKS — THE SECRET INGREDIENT ===

The chard STALKS (better than the leaves) are the secret ingredient — they pair well with the chickpeas. (Same stalks-have-value lesson as [[chard-pickle-pasta]], pointed the other direction: there the leaves lead and the stalks assist; here the stalks are the point.)

=== YELLOW ONIONS ONLY (I THINK) ===

Yellow onions are the onion for this recipe — yellow only, I think.

=== NO OTHER SEASONINGS OR DAIRY REQUIRED ===

Variant B runs on the stock + tomato + chard + bay leaf alone — no additional seasonings, no dairy.

=== WANT TO TRY — LEMON FOR SOURNESS ===

It seems like it could use a bit of sourness — want to try lemon.

=== STANDING CHICKPEA RESCUE ===

If a chickpea dish reads flat/off, the reliable correction is EXTRA CUMIN + LEMON ZEST — works across cuisines.

=== SIBLING RECIPES ===

- [[chana-masala]] / [[himachali-chana-madra]]: the indian tomato/legume chickpea dishes — different family (curry, not stock soup).
- [[sumac-chickpea-skillet]]: the dry-skillet chickpea format.
- [[minestrone-soup]]: the neighboring italian stock-and-legume soup.
- [[chard-pickle-pasta]]: the other swiss-chard recipe — leaves-forward where this is stalks-forward.
why_i_like_this_recipe: Chicken stock + tomato is an unusual combination and it works unreasonably well with chickpeas and swiss chard.
